name: Content Repurposer - RSS to AI social media drafts

nodes.name: 1. RSS Feed Trigger
nodes.notes: Replace with your blog or niche news feed URL. Poll interval is set in the workflow settings after import.

assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value: =You are a social media editor. From the article titled "{{ $json.title }}" ({{ $json.link }}), write: 1) one LinkedIn post (max 120 words, professional, 3 hashtags), 2) one X post (max 240 characters, punchy, 2 hashtags), 3) one short hook line for a video. Return plain text with clear labels.

nodes.name: 5. OpenAI Draft (HTTP)
nodes.notes: Add an HTTP Header Auth credential: name 'Authorization', value 'Bearer YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY'. Swap the model in the body if you prefer.

parameters.jsCode: const j=$input.first().json; const text=j.choices?.[0]?.message?.content||''; return [{json:{ title: $('4. Build AI Prompt').first().json.title, link: $('4. Build AI Prompt').first().json.link, drafts: text, created_at: new Date().toISOString() }}];

nodes.name: 7. Save Drafts to Sheet
nodes.notes: Headers needed: title, link, drafts, created_at. Review drafts in the sheet, copy-paste to post. Human-in-the-loop by design.

nodes.name: 8. Notify on Telegram
nodes.notes: Optional: add your Telegram chat ID and bot credential, or delete this node.

parameters.content:
## What this workflow does

Published a new blog post or article? This workflow turns it into social media drafts for you:

1. It watches your blog's RSS feed and spots each new article.
2. It checks a Google Sheet log so it never drafts the same article twice.
3. It asks AI (OpenAI) to write a LinkedIn post, a short X post, and a one-line video hook from the article.
4. It saves the drafts to your Google Sheet and pings you on Telegram so you can review, tweak, and post them.

You stay in control — it only ever prepares drafts, it never posts anything by itself.

## Setup — do this once before switching it on

1. **Your feed:** open node **1** and replace `https://example.com/feed.xml` with your real RSS feed address (most blogs have one at yoursite.com/feed or /rss).
2. **Draft log Sheet:** create a Google Sheet to store drafts, with headers `title, link, drafts, created_at`. Open nodes **2** and **7**, connect your Google account, and pick that same Sheet in both.
3. **OpenAI key:** open node **5**, and in its Header Auth credential paste your OpenAI API key (from platform.openai.com → API keys). The workflow uses the low-cost `gpt-4o-mini` model; you can change the model name in the node's request body.
4. **Telegram:** open node **8**, connect your Telegram bot credential, and fill in your chat ID so the "drafts ready" ping reaches you. (Don't want the ping? Just delete node **8** — everything else still works.)
5. **Make it yours (optional):** node **4** holds the writing instructions for the AI. Edit the prompt text there to change the tone, the platforms, or the lengths.
6. **How often:** the RSS node checks the feed on the interval set inside node **1** — open it and pick how often suits you.
7. **Test, then activate:** run it once manually, confirm a draft lands in your Sheet, then flip the **Active** toggle.

### 1 · A new article appears

Node **1** watches your RSS feed and brings in new articles. Node **2** reads your draft log Sheet — the list of everything already drafted.

The log is the workflow's memory: if an article is already in there, it will be skipped in the next step, even if the feed shows it again.

### 2 · Draft with AI

Node **3** drops any article whose link is already in the log. Node **4** builds the writing brief: one LinkedIn post, one X post, and one video hook line.

Node **5** sends that brief to OpenAI and gets the three drafts back. Want a different style? Edit the brief in node **4** — no code needed.

### 3 · Clean up the result

Node **6** pulls just the draft text out of OpenAI's reply and pairs it with the article's title and link, plus today's date.

You don't need to change anything here — it just tidies up so the next step can save a clean row.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - 3 Clean up the result

parameters.content:
### 4 · Save & notify

Node **7** saves the drafts as a new row in your Google Sheet — this also adds the article to the log, so it's never drafted twice.

Node **8** then sends you a short Telegram message with the article title and link, so you know fresh drafts are waiting for your review.
